Parametric Plots

interactive_plot accepts any number of named numeric parameters. Plotly creates the graph and native sliders; the shared Plotly.js handler combines their selections in the rendered HTML. The reusable Python helper is in interactive_plot.py, and the HTML bridge is included from plotly_slider.html. All parameter combinations are precomputed, so the HTML size grows with the number of slider values, x points, and plotted series. Pass all series in plots; each entry contains a plotting func, a legend name, and an optional "yaxis": "y2" for the secondary vertical axis. All series receive the same slider parameters. The secondary-axis zero line is disabled so it cannot cover the primary zero line. Use x_range, y_range, and y2_range to fix axis limits, and show_legend=False to hide the legend. Pass Plotly layout options with legend; for example, legend={"x": 0.02, "y": 0.98, "xanchor": "left", "yanchor": "top"} places it inside the upper-left corner. Set show_slider_tick_labels=False to hide the numeric labels beneath the sliders while keeping the selected-value display.
